title: spike: the gh-doors and shell-doors allowlists, prototyped in scratch against the route corpus
why: gh-doors is the riskiest item in the queue (draft-raise took five gate rounds of denylist fixes on the same parser); a scratch prototype run against tests/fixtures/routes.json shows in one sitting whether the allowlists fit their line budgets and leave every seat route where it is.
promise: A run, not a change. In a copy of main made with git archive into a new empty scratch folder, prototype the rules gh-doors and shell-doors promise: (a) gh pr merge reads --admin and --auto through guards._flags; (b) a gh api graphql write whose query WUWEI cannot read (--input -, -F query=@-, an --input file that is missing or not in a plain one-segment command) is refused, and an --input file's query is read for door mutations; (c) any write to a repositories/<id>/... endpoint is refused with a hint to spell repos/<owner>/<repo>; (d) a shlex token made only of the characters ();<>|& that is not a known separator or redirect makes the command unreadable, and so does $' or $" quoting; (e) the ledger pattern also matches .wuwei/ledger and .wuwei with no trailing slash. Then run python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_guards.py (or pytest -q) in the copy and count the runtime lines. Record with `wuwei plan run guard-allowlist-spike --reason "<lines each rule cost, the routes.json rows that moved and why, the suite result>"`. A row that moves to a refusal a seat needs is evidence to narrow gh-doors or shell-doors before they start. Outside: committing anything; the spike's code is thrown away. Real-execution evidence already taken on main fe5bc0b by the lead (stub git on PATH logging argv; real gh 2.89.0 with http_unix_socket pointed at a logging server): bash runs git push origin main for cat <(git push origin main), true;>x git push origin main, true&&(git push origin main), x=1;(git push origin main), git push origin $'main' and $"main"; gh sends POST /graphql with the mutation for --input q.json and for --input -, and POST /repositories/123/pulls/5/requested_reviewers as typed; guards.bash on main passes every one of them. gh pr merge flag shapes were not executed: the merge door refused the probe (correct behaviour), so the merge-flag rules rest on pflag's parsing (a valued short flag takes the next word even when it starts with -).
acceptance: given a git archive copy of main in a new empty scratch folder, when the five prototype rules are applied and tests/test_guards.py runs there, then the run evidence names each rule's runtime line cost and every tests/fixtures/routes.json row whose verdict moved
given the prototype, when the commands in the promise's real-execution list are read by guards.bash, then each is refused, and the run evidence says so command by command
given the spike's outcome, when the planner records it with wuwei plan run, then the reason names the line costs, the moved rows (or none) and the suite result, and no file in the repository changed

title: fix(evidence): a head with no CI checks registered yet reads as CI not started, never as ready to merge
why: Open bug #1085 (labelled bug, opened 2026-10-16 13:25 UTC; G-2 allows three days, so due 2026-10-19): evidence.ci_gaps returns no gap for an empty statusCheckRollup (evidence.py lines 359-370), so a seat can arm auto-merge on an unverified head.
files: docs/site/concepts/evidence.md (if it lists the CI gaps)
promise: Fixes #1085. When a PR head has no check runs and no commit statuses and the repository has run a workflow on pull_request (gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/runs?event=pull_request&per_page=1, cached a day per repository), wuwei evidence reports the safety gap 'CI not started at <sha7>' as waiting (not actionable), never 'no gaps'. An unreadable Actions host counts as having CI, so the gap shows rather than a pass. The merge door holds on it for gh pr merge and for --auto alike: only 'CI running' stays exempt for auto-merge, because GitHub's auto-merge with no required checks merges at once. A repository that never ran a pull_request workflow gets no CI gap, as on main. A gate verdict owed at a moved head is reported whatever the CI state (this holds on main; a test pins it). Touches the files listed. Starts after free-lines-3 (needs runtime room). Rollback: revert the commit; no data or config changes. Outside: CI that runs only on push (its checks already appear in the rollup), required-check settings, the board's wording beyond the new gap text. Assumption: one Actions read per repository per day is cheap enough; overturned if the gh call rate shows in the report.
acceptance: given PR o/r#5 whose head has an empty statusCheckRollup and a repository whose Actions runs list one pull_request run, when wuwei evidence o/r#5 runs with the code host stubbed, then it prints 'CI not started at <sha7>' and not 'no gaps: ready to merge'
given the same PR, when gh pr merge 5 -R o/r --auto --squash is read by guards.bash, then it is refused naming 'CI not started', while a head whose only gap is 'CI running' still passes with --auto
given a repository whose Actions runs list no pull_request run, when the same empty-rollup PR is read, then no CI gap appears, as on main
given the Actions runs read raises GhError, when the empty-rollup PR is read, then 'CI not started at <sha7>' appears

title: fix(hook): PR numbers in owner answers, verdicts, refs and CLI arguments are ASCII digits only
why: Python's \d and str.isdigit() accept Unicode digits and int() converts them, so an owner question naming #７ records a ruling for PR 7: hook.py lines 249 and 281, evidence.py line 52, verdict.py lines 8 and 45, guards.py lines 344 and 349, and __main__._ref line 22 (grep -n '\\d' and isdigit on main fe5bc0b). draft-raise made the guards ASCII-only; these readers were left.
runtime_lines: -2 estimated (the owner review and breaking rulings read one REF match), budget 0: must not grow
promise: Every pattern under cli/wuwei that reads a number uses [0-9] (or re.ASCII), and every isdigit() check is preceded by isascii(), so a PR number written in non-ASCII digits is never read as a PR. The owner review: and breaking: rulings in hook._answers read the same REF match (owner/repo#n at <sha>) instead of two patterns, which frees about 2 lines. A test scans cli/wuwei for \d and for isdigit() without isascii(). Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: \w in repository names; the wording of any message.
acceptance: given an AskUserQuestion answer 'yes' to 'owner review: o/r#７ at abc1234. Approve?', when PostToolUse records it, then no ruling for o/r#7 is written, and with 'o/r#7' it is written as on main

title: fix(guards): gh api graphql queries WUWEI cannot read, repositories/<id> writes, and merge flags read the way gh reads them meet the doors
why: On main fe5bc0b guards.bash passes gh api graphql --input q.json carrying markPullRequestReadyForReview, gh api graphql --input -, and gh api -X POST repositories/123/pulls/5/requested_reviewers, -X PUT repositories/123/pulls/5/merge and contents writes; real gh 2.89.0 sends each of them (logged through http_unix_socket). gh pr merge reads --auto and --admin from raw argv (guards.py lines 195 and 198).
runtime_lines: +5 estimated, budget +8; if headroom at start is below 8 it frees the difference in the same diff
promise: Allowlist plain shapes, never denylist spellings. (1) gh pr merge reads --admin and --auto through guards._flags with merge's value flags: --admin and --admin=<any value gh accepts as true> are refused; --auto counts only when pflag reads it as the auto flag (so in 'gh pr merge 5 -t --auto' it is -t's subject, and the CI-running exemption does not apply); the last --auto wins and --auto=false is off. (2) A gh api graphql call is refused when it could carry a write WUWEI cannot read: --input - or -F query=@-, an --input or -F @ file that is missing, or an --input file in a command that is not one plain segment. An --input file WUWEI reads has its query checked for door mutations like -f query=. (3) Any write method to an endpoint starting repositories/ is refused with a hint to spell repos/<owner>/<repo>/...; reads pass. (4) The redundant len(segments(command) or ()) == 1 clause (guards.py line 208) goes. Each new route is a tests/fixtures/routes.json row naming its source. Acceptance comes from real execution: gh with http_unix_socket pointed at a logging server shows the request each shape sends; merge shapes rest on pflag's parsing because the merge door refuses running them. Starts after guard-allowlist-spike reports, and after free-lines-3 and ascii-digits (guards.py). Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: shell parsing (shell-doors), ready_door comparing the branch by name for fork PRs, repository settings that auto-request reviewers, ?draft=false on a POST (unmeasured: needs GitHub itself). Assumption: no seat route uses gh api graphql --input (none in .wuwei/traces.jsonl's 2,799 rows or routes.json); overturned if the spike or the corpus shows one.
acceptance: given a file q.json holding {"query":"mutation{markPullRequestReadyForReview(input:{pullRequestId:\"X\"}){clientMutationId}}"} and gh pointed by http_unix_socket at a logging server, when gh api graphql --input q.json runs, then the server logs POST /graphql with that mutation, and given the same command, when guards.bash reads it, then it is refused naming markPullRequestReadyForReview

title: fix(guards): process substitution, glued separators, $'...' quoting and ledger paths without a trailing slash meet the doors
why: A stub git on PATH shows bash runs git push origin main for cat <(git push origin main), echo >(...), true;>x git push origin main, true&&(git push origin main), x=1;(git push origin main), git push origin $'main' and $"main"; guards.bash on main fe5bc0b passes all seven, and passes rm -rf .wuwei/ledger, mv .wuwei/ledger x, cp x .wuwei/ledger and rm -rf .wuwei (LEDGER needs a trailing / or .jsonl, guards.py line 30).
runtime_lines: +3 estimated, budget +5; if headroom at start is below 5 it frees the difference in the same diff
promise: Allowlist plain shapes. (1) In guards.segments, a token made only of the characters ();<>|& that is not one of the known separators (CONTROL) or redirects makes the command unreadable (segments returns None), so a command naming a door program is refused by the existing multi-line or unreadable rule; a command naming none still passes. (2) $' and $" quoting in a command naming a door program makes it unreadable the same way. (3) The ledger pattern matches .wuwei/ledger and .wuwei/ledger.jsonl with or without a trailing slash, and .wuwei itself, as a writer argument, redirect target or edit path, so rm, mv, cp, tee, dd and the rest naming them are refused. Each shape is a tests/fixtures/routes.json row or a test case. Acceptance comes from real execution with a stub program on PATH that logs its argv. Starts after gh-doors (guards.py). Rollback: revert the commit. Outside: a ledger write after cd .wuwei (cwd is not tracked), find -delete, git clean, and wrappers beyond those guards.py lists; these stay recorded gaps. Assumption: no seat route puts a door program inside process substitution or $'...'; overturned if the corpus moves a recorded route.
acceptance: given a stub git on PATH that appends its argv to a log, when bash -c runs each of cat <(git push origin main), echo >(git push origin main), true;>x git push origin main, true&&(git push origin main), x=1;(git push origin main), git push origin $'main' and git push origin $"main", then the log holds 'push origin main' each time, and given each command, when guards.bash reads it, then it is refused
